clue.text: Fairy story recalled in new version

indicators.note: a new version of something is a reworking, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A classic fairy tale is remembered and retold in a modern adaptation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' looks like part of the surface story of remembering, but it is fodder: the letters of RECALLED plus IN are rearranged, with 'new version' as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The rags-to-riches tale of the girl, the glass slipper and the pumpkin coach is one of the best-known fairy tales.

clue.text: Uncertain of moment judge left

indicators.note: left is read as 'departed', so the judge's letter goes away from the word for a moment

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment, a very short time

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure whether the judge left at the crucial moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is not the opposite of right here but 'departed': J leaves JIFFY.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something doubtful or questionable is described as dodgy or chancy in this way.

clue.text: One herding animals right into port

indicators.note: into tells us one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: Dover is the English Channel port in Kent

explanation.surface: A herdsman drives his livestock straight into a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: DOVER is England's main ferry port to France; R goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A drover is a person who drives cattle or sheep to market over long distances.

clue.text: Have qualms again about fieldwork

explanation.surface: Someone doubts once more whether the outdoor research is worthwhile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fieldwork' suggests research outdoors, but it is a military term for a temporary fortification built in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-doubt it means to feel misgivings a second time; as a noun it is a small detached fort or earthwork.

clue.text: The French hold old boy by part of ear

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so the French article wraps around the other piece

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
OB is the usual abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: The French grab a former pupil by the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleshy lower part of the outer ear, where earrings go, has this name.

clue.text: Approaches between the trees

explanation.surface: Paths into a place run through the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: An avenue is both a way of approach (avenues of inquiry) and a road lined with trees on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads or ways leading somewhere, often wide streets flanked by rows of trees.

clue.text: Dividing lodging

explanation.surface: Splitting up living quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting into four parts, and also providing soldiers with billets or accommodation.

clue.text: Spectator who may be needed on stand

definitions.text: who may be needed on stand

explanation.surface: An onlooker who might have to give evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand' is the witness box in a court, not a spectator stand at a sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who saw an event happen, and a person called to testify about it in court.

clue.text: Youngster heard mark for navigation

indicators.note: heard means we listen to how a word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a boy is a youngster

explanation.surface: A child listened to a navigational marker.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating marker anchored at sea to guide ships or warn of hazards.

clue.text: Within one's means, it's pleasant to hold gold and diamonds

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so the word for pleasant wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: affable means pleasant and friendly
OR is gold in heraldry
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Gold and diamonds within your budget would be a pleasant thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold' is not jewellery here but the heraldic tincture; 'to hold' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheap enough that you can pay for it without strain.

clue.text: Exclusive new dart

parts.note: a dart is a small arrow

explanation.surface: A select new dart.
explanation.definitionFit: Restricted or limited in scope, as in a narrow interpretation that excludes much.

clue.text: Germ man injected into lab animals

indicators.note: injected into tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: mice are common laboratory animals
Rob is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man injects a germ into laboratory mice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny organism such as a bacterium, especially one that causes disease.

clue.text: Insist on principle to put up seating

explanation.surface: Someone holds firm on principle by building somewhere to sit.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a firm position on an issue, and literally to construct a stand for spectators.

clue.text: Black and white issues are settled here

definitions.text: Black and white issues are settled here

parts.words: Black and white issues are settled here
parts.note: issues in black and white suggests clear-cut questions, but here they are contests between the dark and light pieces of a board game played on chequered squares

explanation.surface: A place where clear-cut questions are resolved.
explanation.definitionFit: The chequered board of 64 squares on which the game between black and white pieces is fought out.

clue.text: "Bird" is better than "birdie"

explanation.surface: A bird beats a little bird.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf a birdie is one under par, and this score, two under par, beats it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bird of prey, and in golf a hole played two strokes under par.

clue.text: One's late leaving

parts.note: late leaving suggests a delayed departure, but late means dead and leaving means what is left in a will

explanation.surface: Someone departs behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy, something left to someone in a will by a person now deceased.

clue.text: Objection about service is overdone

indicators.note: about means around, so the objection wraps the other piece

parts.note: a 'but' is an objection, as in no ifs or buts
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the tennis serve has been overdone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests tennis or a meal, but it is one of the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooked too long until charred, as overdone food is.

clue.text: Put name to American river

parts.note: to tag something is to put a label or name on it

explanation.surface: Naming an American river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tagus is the longest river of the Iberian peninsula, flowing through Spain to Lisbon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tagus is a long Iberian waterway reaching the sea at Lisbon.

clue.text: Was aware monarch went to Oxford college

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, a monarch
New College is one of the colleges of Oxford University

explanation.surface: Someone knew the king had attended an Oxford college.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of to know, so had knowledge of something.

clue.text: From diving position, spear fish

explanation.surface: A diver spears a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackknife diving posture with straight legs, an old infantry weapon with a long shaft, and a predatory freshwater fish.

clue.text: About noon 1do bunk from Welsh town

indicators.note: about means around, so the flight wraps around the other piece

parts.note: to do a bunk is British slang for running away, to flit

explanation.surface: Around midday someone runs away from a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: To do a bunk is British slang for leaving in secret. Flint is a town in north-east Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Flint is a town in north Wales on the Dee estuary, giving its name to Flintshire.

clue.text: Girl from the country, with son

parts.note: France is a country

explanation.surface: A girl comes from the countryside with her son.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Sweet finally to embrace many times over

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word sweet

parts.note: to enfold someone is to embrace them

explanation.surface: Sweet things at last hug you many times over.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiplied by ten, hence greatly increased.

clue.text: Tea sure to be drunk to get sober

indicators.note: drunk suggests something muddled, so the letters of tea sure get rearranged

explanation.surface: A cup of tea is sure to sober you up.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and plain, without luxury, like a serious and restrained manner.

clue.text: Crying shame if police have to fire this?

definitions.text: Crying shame if police have to fire this?

parts.words: Crying shame if police have to fire this?
parts.note: a crying shame is a pity, but here read literally: a weapon police fire to make crowds shed tears

explanation.surface: It would be a pity if officers had to shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical spray used by riot police that irritates the eyes and makes people weep.

clue.text: From Nevada divorce centre I run to artist

parts.note: Reno in Nevada was famous for quick divorces
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone flees a Nevada divorce town for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Mythical horse, a hard worker

explanation.surface: A legendary horse that works very hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The wooden horse of Troy; to work like a Trojan means to work very hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek wooden horse at Troy, and someone diligent, as in working like one.

clue.text: Make pounds out of toy

parts.note: to do is to make, as in do a drawing
L is an abbreviation for a pound sterling, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Making money out of a plaything.
explanation.definitionFit: A small figure of a person used as a child's plaything.

clue.text: Tilt table

explanation.surface: A sloping table.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's lean to one side, and a written series of items such as a catalogue or schedule.

clue.text: One always at bar, hav, ing nibbles?

definitions.text: One always at bar, hav, ing nibbles

parts.words: One always at bar, hav, ing nibbles
parts.note: always at the bar suggests a drinker snacking in a pub, but the bar is one of sweets and the nibbles are its squares

explanation.surface: A regular at the pub who is always eating snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A person addicted to the sweet treat made from cocoa, by analogy with an alcoholic.

clue.text: Annoy police informer

explanation.surface: Irritating a police grass.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang both for to irritate and for a person who tells tales to the police.

clue.text: Team spirit is adroitly refocussed

indicators.note: refocussed suggests the letters are brought together in a new order

explanation.surface: Team spirit is cleverly given a new focus.
explanation.definitionFit: Unity of purpose and mutual support among members of a group.
